headline: High-risk workspace and MCP overlap: Continue can write/read shared files and use MCP, while the paired repo is a docs-only content source with no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can use MCP and reads workspace files/editor buffers, so malicious content in shared files or MCP outputs could be treated as instructions. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a content repository with no isolation or provenance controls, so if its material is fed into Continue, prompt injection is plausible. The pathway is interaction-based and not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is copied into agent_b's workspace or MCP context
IF agent_b parses file or MCP content as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable MCP for the session
Keep agent_a content in a read-only, separate folder
Add a manual instruction/content delimiter before pasting
Review any imported snippets before sending them to agent_b

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue reads and writes workspace files and shares state via filesystem across instances, so data placed in the workspace can flow between agents. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is docs-only and does not itself expose sensitive data, but the pair can still leak editor buffers or source code if those are stored in the shared workspace. The shared filesystem makes the pathway default-feasible.
conditions: IF sensitive editor buffers or source code are stored in the shared workspace
IF multiple Continue instances access the same filesystem-backed state
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Exclude secrets and private files from the shared folder
Turn off syncing of editor buffers to shared storage
Rotate any exposed API keys if they were opened in the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has write_filesystem, execute_shell, install_packages, and broad network egress, while the paired repo is a static content source with no write capability. There is no direct write-write conflict with agent_a, but Continue’s filesystem sharing across instances means concurrent edits can collide if the repo is used as a workspace. Uncertainty about the repo’s runtime role pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a content is placed in the same writable workspace used by agent_b
IF multiple Continue instances edit the same files without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate directory
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Use git branches or patches instead of direct writes
Pause one instance before the other writes shared files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on MCP/tool outputs and the profile says tool calls require user approval, but its chat/autocomplete flow can still consume prior content as context. If material from Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is treated as authoritative guidance, downstream actions or code changes may reflect unverified advice. The pair lacks a verification boundary, so cascading error is plausible though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF agent_a-derived guidance is pasted into agent_b as authoritative context
IF agent_b uses that context to generate code or tool calls without independent verification
mitigations: Require a second review before acting on imported guidance
Mark imported snippets as untrusted
Ask agent_b to cite source URLs before using advice
Limit tool use until outputs are checked manually

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for either agent, and agent_a is a docs-only repository while agent_b handles source code and editor buffers. Because the profiles do not show regulated data classes or conflicting compliance regimes, only a low residual compliance risk remains from generic logging/retention uncertainty. The other agent is not cited beyond its docs-only status because no specific compliance surface is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_b's workspace
IF logging or retention policies differ for the same data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Review logging settings for editor buffers
Store secrets in a dedicated secret manager
Document retention rules before use
